    14  /-!
    15  # Deterministic Finite Automata
    16  
    17  A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) is a state machine which
    18  decides membership in a particular `Language`, by following a path
    19  uniquely determined by an input string.
    20  
    21  We define regular languages to be ones for which a DFA exists, other formulations
    22  are later proved equivalent.
    23  
    24  Note that this definition allows for automata with infinite states,
    25  a `Fintype` instance must be supplied for true DFAs.
    26  
    27  ## Main definitions
    28  
    29  - `DFA α σ`: automaton over alphabet `α` and set of states `σ`
    30  - `M.accepts`: the language accepted by the DFA `M`
    31  - `Language.IsRegular L`: a predicate stating that `L` is a regular language, i.e. there exists
    32    a DFA that recognizes the language
    33  
    34  ## Main theorems
    35  
    36  - `DFA.pumping_lemma` : every sufficiently long string accepted by the DFA has a substring that can
    37    be repeated arbitrarily many times (and have the overall string still be accepted)
    38  
    39  ## Implementation notes
    40  
    41  Currently, there are two disjoint sets of simp lemmas: one for `DFA.eval`, and another for
    42  `DFA.evalFrom`. You can switch from the former to the latter using `simp [eval]`.

    56  /-- A DFA is a set of states (`σ`), a transition function from state to state labelled by the
    57    alphabet (`step`), a starting state (`start`) and a set of acceptance states (`accept`). -/
    58  structure DFA (α : Type u) (σ : Type v) where
    59    /-- A transition function from state to state labelled by the alphabet. -/
    60    step : σ → α → σ
    61    /-- Starting state. -/
    62    start : σ
    63    /-- Set of acceptance states. -/
    64    accept : Set σ

    66  namespace DFA

    68  variable {α : Type u} {σ : Type v} (M : DFA α σ)
